personas.name: Aoife, hiring manager
personas.role: Engineering manager at a software company in Dublin
personas.goal: Shortlist graduate engineers quickly and see real evidence of skills
personas.frustration: Portfolios that hide the actual work behind long text
personas.scenario: Aoife has two minutes between interviews. She opens the link from a CV on her phone, wants to see the projects first, filters them by .NET, opens one case study and checks the GitHub activity before deciding to call.

personas.name: Dr Saay, module assessor
personas.goal: Check every brief item and rubric line, and trace each change to a commit
personas.frustration: Having to search the repository to find where something is done
personas.scenario: The assessor opens the live site from Brightspace, goes to the Readme page, follows the peer-review table to the commits, checks that the CI/CD pipeline is green, and tries search, filters and the offline mode.

personas.name: Rahul, fellow MSc student
personas.role: International student at UL, new to Ireland
personas.goal: Ask questions and share tips with other students
personas.frustration: No simple way to reach a classmate outside college channels
personas.scenario: Rahul reads a blog post about the move to Limerick, asks the chat assistant how to get in touch, and leaves a comment in the community feed. On the bus with no signal he opens the installed site again to re-read the post.

stories.story: As a hiring manager, I want to see projects first, so that I can judge skills fast.
As a hiring manager, I want to filter work by technology, so that I only read what matches the role.
As a hiring manager, I want to see recent GitHub activity, so that I know the skills are current.
As the assessor, I want a Readme page that explains the structure, so that I can mark without reading every file.
As the assessor, I want every change linked to a commit and a review point, so that I can verify the work.
As the assessor, I want to see that tests run automatically on every push, so that I can trust the quality.
As the assessor, I want to find any topic with one search, so that I can check a rubric item quickly.
As a student, I want to ask a question and get an instant answer, so that I do not wait for an email.
As a student, I want to comment on a post, so that I can share my own tips.
As a student on the move, I want the site to open without a connection, so that I can re-read posts on the bus.
As a visitor on a slow phone, I want pages to load fast and move smoothly, so that the site feels professional.

features.name: Home page: introduction, key numbers, featured projects, career path
About: story, quick facts, roles, experience timeline
Education: qualifications timeline, certifications
Professional Knowledge: case studies, projects, skills
Pictures gallery: category filter and full-size viewer
Video gallery: player and playlist with local video files
Blog: articles with tag filter
Community feed: posts, images, likes, comments
Instant messaging: auto-reply assistant and live lounge
Search across pages and case studies
URL routing with NotFound and deep links
Navigation bar on every page, mobile menu
One hand-written responsive stylesheet with dark mode
Typed data and reusable components
Strict TypeScript check in every build
API server: hashed passwords, protected delete
Readme page describing the structure
Hosted API so every visitor shares one feed
Database instead of JSON files on the server
Real-time messaging across devices (WebSockets)
Admin role to moderate posts and messages
Live GitHub data: repositories and pipeline runs from the GitHub API
Content in JSON files loaded at run time (dynamic data)
Unit, component, API and browser tests in CI
Accessibility audit (WCAG 2.2 AA) and video captions
Lazy loading: pages, images and animation library on demand
CI/CD pipeline with GitHub Actions and deployment to GitHub Pages
GSAP animations and interactive elements
Smart search: ranked, typo-tolerant, filters by type, highlights matches; concept location in the source code
Installable offline app (Progressive Web App)
Code quality dashboard generated by the pipeline
Modular feature folders with hooks; JSDoc on every file
Personas, scenarios and user stories traced to features
